title: Decide npm scope and versioning for the tektonic-ci packages
description:
Two decisions every later step depends on.

1. Scope: keep @pfenerty/tektonic, @pfenerty/tektonic-cache-gcs, @pfenerty/tektonic-reporter-github, or move to an @tektonic-ci npm org (e.g. @tektonic-ci/core, @tektonic-ci/cache-gcs, @tektonic-ci/reporter-github). A scope change is a rename: new package names, the old ones get npm deprecate pointing at the new, consumers change imports. Recommendation: move to @tektonic-ci now, once, alongside the repo move, rather than a second disruption later; the org is the paradigm. Requires creating the npm org and adding the maintainer.
2. Versioning: packages are lockstep at 2.0.1 today. After the split, version independently; providers declare a peerDependency on core's major (^2) and bump only when they change. Record whether the first release under a new scope restarts at 1.0.0 or continues at 2.x (continuing avoids implying a reset of the API).

Record both decisions in docs/adr/ in core.
acceptance_criteria: ADR merged in core recording scope and versioning; npm org created if scope changes.
notes: 2026-09-26 decided (user): scope @tektonic-ci/* with package = @<org>/<repo> (@tektonic-ci/core, @tektonic-ci/reporter-github, @tektonic-ci/cache-gcs); continue the 2.x line (core's first release under the new name is 2.1.0); version independently after the split, with providers declaring a peer dependency on @tektonic-ci/core ^2. ADR 0002 in PR #78. Left for a human: create the tektonic-ci npm org. Close once #78 merges and the org exists.
close_reason: ADR 0002 merged (#78); the tektonic-ci npm org is created (registry /-/org/tektonic-ci returns 200).

title: Move to the tektonic-ci GitHub org: core repo + one repo per provider package

They still live in one npm-workspaces monorepo (pfenerty/tektonic), built with tsc project references and published by one workflow, so 'a provider is just a package anyone could write' is asserted, not demonstrated.

Deliver the paradigm physically, under the new tektonic-ci GitHub org:
- pfenerty/tektonic -> tektonic-ci/core (transfer + rename, keeps history, issues, redirects)
- packages/tektonic-reporter-github -> tektonic-ci/reporter-github
- packages/tektonic-cache-gcs -> tektonic-ci/cache-gcs
Each provider repo builds, tests, self-CIs (via tektonic, PAC) and publishes on its own against the published core, exactly as a third-party provider would.

Touches: tektonic (this repo), homelab (PAC Repository CRs, GitHub App, renovate cronjob), ocidex + homelab .tektonic (package deps if the npm scope changes), npmjs.com (trusted publishers). Beads for the whole initiative live here since this backlog moves with the repo to tektonic-ci/core.
acceptance_criteria: Three repos under tektonic-ci each green in self-CI and each publishing via its own trusted publisher; core has no in-tree provider packages; ocidex and homelab consume the packages from npm under the chosen scope; no live reference to pfenerty/tektonic outside redirects and history.

title: Ship a tektonic CLI: synth, check, graph, lint
description:
Every consumer reimplements synth and drift-check. In ocidex that is: make tekton-synth and make tekton-check (Makefile:173-184), a bespoke ~30-line tekton-check Tekton task (.tektonic/jobs/tekton-check/spec.ts), AND a TEKTON_OUTDIR environment hack threaded into the project definition itself (.tektonic/pipeline.ts:133) purely so the drift check can synth to a throwaway dir and diff it.

Drift-check in particular belongs in the library rather than in each consumer: ocidex hand-rolled version used exit 1 inside a nushell body, which the exit-code contract swallows, so it reported GREEN ON DRIFT for months (ocidex-im4o.1). A library command gets that right once.

Commands: synth (build the project), check (synth to a temp dir and diff against the committed output, non-zero on drift or orphaned files), graph (render the task DAG for review), lint (run the existing scripts/lint-scripts.cjs over extracted script files — today it is an internal npm script consumers cannot reach).
design: Add a bin entry to package.json. check does a recursive diff so it also catches orphans — files the project no longer emits — which a git-status-based check misses (see the ocidex Makefile comment). Once check exists, outdir redirection is a CLI flag and the TEKTON_OUTDIR env hack can leave consumer code.
acceptance_criteria: npx tektonic check exits non-zero on a stale or hand-edited output dir and zero on a clean one. ocidex Makefile targets and its tekton-check task body reduce to CLI invocations.
notes:
CLI implemented and committed (src/cli/, docs/cli.md, bin entry in package.json). Verified end to end against examples/self-ci.ts. Remains open only because it is blocked by tektonic-k2n.8 (registry publish): until the package is published, consumers reach the CLI via the git dependency rather than npx tektonic.
2026-09-25: ocidex migration in pfenerty/ocidex#145 (ocidex-jfp0): Makefile targets + tekton-check task body are now tektonic synth/check, TEKTON_OUTDIR removed. Verified locally clean→0, stale+orphan→1. Close when #145 merges green.

title: Publish @pfenerty/tektonic to a registry; drop the git-dependency install path
description:
README tells consumers to run npm install @pfenerty/tektonic, but nothing is published. ocidex installs github:pfenerty/tektonic#v1.4.0 (.tektonic/package.json), which drags two workarounds into CI, both in .tektonic/jobs/tekton-check/spec.ts:
- git config --global url.https://github.com/.insteadOf ssh://git@github.com/ because npm normalizes github: deps to git+ssh in the lockfile and CI has no SSH key;
- npm ci --allow-git=all because npm 12+ defaults allow-git to none and blocks the git dependency outright.
It also means every consumer install compiles TypeScript via the prepare script, and consumers need a git client plus network access to github.com in the build image.

Publishing to npmjs or GitHub Packages deletes all of that.
design: Publish from the existing release flow. Decide npmjs (public, simplest for consumers) vs GitHub Packages (needs an auth line in consumer .npmrc). Files array in package.json is already correct. Update README, ocidex/.tektonic/package.json, homelab/tekton-pipelines/package.json, and drop the two git workarounds from the ocidex tekton-check task.
acceptance_criteria: npm install @pfenerty/tektonic works from a clean checkout with no git config; ocidex tekton-check task runs a plain npm ci.
notes: Released 2.0.1 via staged trusted publishing (tektonic-k2n.18). ocidex migration in pfenerty/ocidex#144 (ocidex-9cf6) — close this when it merges and CI is green. homelab/tekton-pipelines depends on the older @pfenerty/tekton-pipelines package (github:pfenerty/tekton-pipelines), not tektonic — separate migration, filed in homelab.

title: Cache restore rm -rf s paths in use by concurrent tasks on a shared workspace
description:
The PVC backend restore step deletes the cache paths before extracting. ocidex points GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE at .go-mod/.go-build INSIDE the shared source workspace (.tektonic/shared.ts:129-142), so those paths are live for every concurrent Go task in the run.

Production incident (ocidex-plh, run ocidex-ocidex-push-hh77k): a govulncheck-scan restore landed mid-build; openapi-verify died with package encoding/json is not in std when the module cache vanished under it, and govulncheck own rm -rf failed ENOTEMPTY against openapi-verify still writing. Documented at .tektonic/shared.ts:91-105.

The workaround is four near-identical cache specs — goCache, goCacheTest, goCacheVulncheck, goCacheIntegration (shared.ts:72-117) — differing only in skipRestoreIfPathsExist / forceSave, each carrying a paragraph of incident archaeology.
design: In order of value: (a) make restore atomic — extract to a temp dir and rename into place, never rm -rf a live path; (b) at synth time, detect that a cache paths resolve inside a workspace shared with other tasks in the same pipeline and default skipRestoreIfPathsExist: true with a warning; (c) model warm-cache producer/consumer as one declaration so the four hand-derived spreads collapse to one.
acceptance_criteria: Two tasks sharing a workspace and a cache can run concurrently without one destroying the other paths. ocidex can drop at least two of its four cache spreads.
close_reason: Atomic staged restore + shared-workspace detection landed; producer/consumer modeling split out as a follow-up

title: gated() Proxy breaks task identity — non-leaf tasks cannot be gated
description:
gated() returns a Proxy (src/lib/core/pipeline-task.ts:74-101), but Pipeline.discoverAllTasks dedupes by object identity via Set<TaskLike> (pipeline.ts:122-131). The Proxy is a distinct object from its target, so when any other task holds needs: [rawTask], discovery collects BOTH the proxy and the raw task, both report the same name, and validate() throws duplicate task name (pipeline.ts:237-243). runAfterFor has the same identity bug: this.allTasks.includes(dep) misses when the pipeline holds the proxy and the dependent holds the raw task (pipeline.ts:214-216), which silently drops the ordering edge.

Net effect: only LEAF tasks can be gated. Costs observed in ocidex:
- .tektonic/jobs/go-integration/spec.ts:15-21 — goIntegration must depend on goBuild rather than the cheaper-to-fail goTest, purely to avoid the collision.
- .tektonic/pipeline.ts:76-81 — goBuild and frontendLint run on EVERY PR, including frontend-only and docs-only ones, because they are depended upon and therefore ungatable. This is real wasted CI on the single-worker cluster.
design: Replace the Proxy with an identity-preserving overlay. gated() returns a marker object { task, overrides }; Pipeline unwraps markers into a Map<TaskLike, PipelineTaskOverrides> before discovery, so identity dedupes to the underlying task, and applies the overrides in _buildSpec / _toPipelineTaskSpec. Call-site compatible: gated() results are only ever passed inside a tasks: array. effectiveWhen() in pipeline.ts:16-19 reads the overlay map instead of poking _overrides through the proxy.
acceptance_criteria: A task that other tasks depend on can be gated in one pipeline and ungated in another; the emitted pipeline has one entry for it with the correct when and correct runAfter edges. Regression test covering the goBuild/goTest shape.

title: Reporting tasks killed by OOM/eviction/timeout leave GitHub checks pending forever
description:
createSkipResolverTask is only emitted for tasks that have a when (pipeline.ts:100-108) and only acts on Tekton status None (github-status-reporter.ts:185-193). Any reporting task killed at the infrastructure level — OOMKill, node eviction, image-pull failure, TaskRun timeout — never reaches its report-status step, so the context set by set-status-pending stays pending forever with no signal.

ocidex pays for this in application code: memoryWatchdog() (.tektonic/script-lib.ts:20-63) is 28 lines of POSIX sh that polls the container cgroup memory.current against memory.max and self-terminates the child at 92 percent, converting a would-be OOMKill into an ordinary exit 99 that onError: continue can handle. Wired into semgrep-sast and govulncheck-scan. Its comment states the reason exactly: an OOMKill bypasses onError: continue entirely because Tekton treats it as an infrastructure failure.
design: Emit the finally reconciler for EVERY reporting task, not only gated ones. Map None to success/skipped (current behaviour) and Failed-without-a-report to failure. The resolver already receives the per-task status as a param via Param.pipelineExpression (statusParam), so the mechanism is in place — only the selection predicate and the status branch need widening. An optional built-in OOM guard step wrapper can follow as a separate issue.
acceptance_criteria: A pipeline where a reporting task is OOMKilled ends with that GitHub context red, not pending. Verified by an ad-hoc TaskRun/PipelineRun with a deliberately over-limit step.

title: Foundation hardening: correctness seams, CLI/distribution, scripting ergonomics
description:
Assessment of tektonic v1.4.0 using ocidex/.tektonic (~1400 lines across pipeline.ts, shared.ts, script-lib.ts, changes.ts and 16 job specs) as the reference consumer.

The library is solid: coherent Param/Workspace/Result/Task/Pipeline model, real strategy interfaces (CacheBackend, StatusReporter, ScriptLanguage), scripts as lintable files, ~4.6k source vs ~3.3k test lines, schema validation against the Tekton v1 swagger.

The gap is that the seams a consumer actually leans on -- gating, status completeness, cache sharing, script composition, distribution -- each have a sharp edge that ocidex routed around in application code. Nearly every multi-paragraph comment in ocidex's pipeline code marks one, and several mark production incidents (ocidex-plh, ocidex-im4o.1, ocidex-qzz2, semgrep-4pf).

Scope boundary: tektonic stays a FOUNDATION. Reusable job libraries (SARIF upload, syft/grype scans, buildkit builds) are built ON tektonic, not INTO it. Children under 'foundation seams' are about providing the extension points such a library needs, not absorbing it.

Full assessment: ~/.claude/plans/evaluate-the-current-state-velvet-kazoo.md
notes:
15/17 children closed. k2n.8 (npm publish) and k2n.9 (CLI) are implemented and merged but stay open until the first publish: the npm-token secret must be created in the tektonic-ci namespace and a v2.0.0 tag pushed. package.json is bumped to 2.0.0 as of dec7fec.

Remaining tektonic follow-ups outside this epic: tektonic-ltm (warm-cache producer/consumer; blocks ocidex goCache consolidation), tektonic-acw (synth --prune), tektonic-atb.

title: Fix: when-gated statusReporter tasks stuck on pending status
description: Tasks with a statusReporter and a when condition (via TaskOptions.when or gated()) that get skipped by Tekton never run their embedded report-status step, leaving the GitHub commit status stuck on pending forever. Add a finally-block resolver task that checks $(tasks.<name>.status) and resolves skipped contexts to success/Skipped.

title: PACProject: per-pipeline set-status-pending name collision
description: All pipelines name their pending task 'set-status-pending'; PACProject dedupes by name and emits one, so multi-pipeline projects share the wrong pending task (PR pipeline marks push-only contexts pending and never resolves them). Make the pending task name pipeline-scoped.

Define CacheBackend strategy interface; convert PVC + GCS to implementations
description:
## Why
Now that PVC and GCS live in their own modules, define the `CacheBackend`
strategy interface and have `TaskDef` delegate to it. This removes the
`if (backend.type === 'gcs')` branching from `task.ts` and makes new backends
purely additive — the keystone of the E4 refactor.

## What to change
- File: `src/lib/core/cache-backend.ts`.
  - Replace the existing union type with a real interface:
    ```ts
    export interface CacheBackend {
      /** Discriminator used by the existing config UI ('gcs', 'pvc', ...). */
      readonly type: string;
      /** Returns the step that restores the cache at the start of the task. */
      restoreStep(spec: TaskCacheSpec, taskName: string, ctx: BackendCtx): TaskStepSpec;
      /** Returns the step that saves the cache at the end of the task. */
      saveStep(spec: TaskCacheSpec, taskName: string, ctx: BackendCtx): TaskStepSpec;
    }
    export interface BackendCtx {
      defaultBaseImage: string;
      defaultGcsCacheImage: string;
    }
    ```
- File: `src/lib/cache/pvc-backend.ts`.
  - Export `class PvcBackend implements CacheBackend { type = 'pvc'; ... }`.
- File: `src/lib/cache/gcs-backend.ts`.
  - Convert the GCS config to a class: `GcsBackend implements CacheBackend`.
  - Keep the user-facing config shape (`{ type: 'gcs', bucket, prefix }`)
    accepted via a factory function so existing user code keeps working — e.g.
    `gcs({ bucket, prefix })` returns a `GcsBackend` instance.
- File: `src/lib/core/task.ts`.
  - Delete `_makeCacheRestoreStep` and `_makeCacheSaveStep`.
  - Inline the dispatch as `c.backend.restoreStep(c, this.name, ctx)`.
  - Default backend when `c.backend` is undefined: a `new PvcBackend()`.

## Acceptance
- `flox activate -- npm test` passes.
- `grep "backend.type === " src/` returns no matches.
- Generated YAML for both PVC and GCS examples is byte-identical to pre-refactor.

## Hints
- This is the highest-risk issue in E4 because it changes the user-facing shape
  slightly (`backend: { type: 'gcs', ... }` → `backend: gcs({...})`). Provide
  the factory function `gcs()` so both styles work via a type guard if needed.

## Depends on
- T4.1, T4.2.

title: Epic: TaskLike abstraction (split Task into TaskLike + TaskDef + TaskRef)
description:
## Why
Today the `Task` class does double duty: it is both a Task *spec* (synthesized
as a `kind: Task` Kubernetes resource) AND the only node type a Pipeline can
reference. This conflation blocks ArtifactHub interop: there is no way to express
"this pipeline node is a remote, hub-resolved Task" because every node is assumed
to be locally synthesizable.

This epic introduces a `TaskLike` interface so Pipeline can operate on
heterogeneous nodes (local definitions, hub references, cluster tasks). It is the
foundation for E3 (HubTaskRef), and removes the structural barrier to ecosystem
integration called out in the evaluation document.

Reference: `/Users/patrickfenerty/.claude/plans/evaluate-this-code-repoistory-federated-nest.md`,
priority #1.

## Scope
- New `TaskLike` interface capturing what Pipeline needs from a node.
- Rename existing `Task` class to `TaskDef`; keep `Task` as a type alias for back-compat.
- Update Pipeline, GitPipeline, TektonProject to operate on `TaskLike[]` and skip
  resource synth for nodes that are not `TaskDef`.

## Out of scope
- HubTaskRef / ClusterTaskRef implementations (handled in E3).
- Results (E2), `when` (E5), cache backends (E4), VCS providers (E6).

## Done when
- All four child issues closed.
- `flox activate -- npm test` passes.
- Existing `examples/main.ts` and `examples/self-ci.ts` synth byte-identical YAML.

title: Define TaskLike interface; rename Task class to TaskDef; keep Task as alias
description:
## Why
Introduces the `TaskLike` interface and renames `Task` to `TaskDef` so the
codebase can describe Pipeline nodes that are not locally-synthesized resources.
First step of the E1 keystone refactor.

## What to change
- File: `src/lib/core/task.ts`.
  - Add `TaskLike` interface above the `Task` class:
    ```ts
    export interface TaskLike {
      readonly name: string;
      readonly params: Param[];
      readonly workspaces: Workspace[];
      /** True when this node synthesizes its own `kind: Task` resource. */
      readonly synthesizable: boolean;
      _toPipelineTaskSpec(runAfterNames: string[], namePrefix?: string): Record<string, unknown>;
    }
    ```
  - Rename `export class Task` → `export class TaskDef implements TaskLike`.
  - Add `readonly synthesizable = true;` field.
  - Below the class, add: `export const Task = TaskDef; export type Task = TaskDef;`
    (or use namespace pattern) so existing `new Task({...})` code keeps working.
- File: `src/index.ts`.
  - Export `TaskLike` type alongside `Task`/`TaskDef`.

## Acceptance
- `flox activate -- npm run build` succeeds.
- `flox activate -- npm test` passes — no test changes should be required.
- `grep -R "instanceof Task\b" src/` returns no matches that would break under
  the rename, OR all such matches are updated to `TaskDef`.

## Hints
- Mirror the pattern of `StatusReporter` for the interface shape — small,
  intentional, only what callers need.
- The `Task` static `_makePvcRestoreScript` etc. methods stay on `TaskDef`
  unchanged for now — they'll be extracted in E4.

title: Update Pipeline + GitPipeline to operate on TaskLike[]
description:
## Why
Pipeline's `discoverAllTasks`, `inferParams`, `inferWorkspaces`, and validation
logic must accept any `TaskLike`, not just `TaskDef`. Without this, HubTaskRef
(E3) cannot be a pipeline node.

## What to change
- File: `src/lib/core/pipeline.ts`.
  - Change all `Task` references in field/parameter types to `TaskLike` where the
    code only reads `name`, `params`, `workspaces`, or calls
    `_toPipelineTaskSpec` / has `needs`.
  - Keep `needs: TaskLike[]` (move the `needs` field declaration from `Task` to
    `TaskLike`, or accept it as a separate concept — see hints).
  - `discoverAllTasks` traverses `needs`, so `TaskLike.needs: TaskLike[]` must
    exist. Add `needs: TaskLike[]` to the interface in `task.ts`.
- File: `src/lib/core/git-pipeline.ts`.
  - Update `_discoverUserTasks` signature to `TaskLike[]`.

## Acceptance
- `flox activate -- npm test` — all existing pipeline tests pass.
- `flox activate -- npm run build` — clean compile.

## Hints
- This is a pure type-widening refactor. No behavior change.
- The status-reporter pending task logic in `Pipeline` constructor reads
  `t.statusContext` and `t.statusReporter` — those stay specific to `TaskDef`.
  Type-narrow with `instanceof TaskDef` before accessing them.
- Don't push `synthesizable` into `Pipeline`'s logic yet — that's T1.3's job.

## Depends on
- T1.1 (TaskLike interface must exist first).

title: TektonProject: skip resource synth for non-synthesizable TaskLikes
description:
## Why
`TektonProject` currently calls `task.synth(...)` for every task it collects.
For `TaskLike` nodes that are not synthesizable (e.g. a future HubTaskRef), this
would crash. Filter by `synthesizable` before synthesizing.

## What to change
- File: `src/lib/core/tekton-project.ts`.
  - In the "Collect unique Tasks across all pipelines" loop, only include nodes
    where `task.synthesizable` is true (or `task instanceof TaskDef`).
  - In the "Synth each unique Task" loop, only synthesize those nodes.

## Acceptance
- `flox activate -- npm test` — all existing project tests pass.
- Manually verify with `examples/main.ts`: synthesized output unchanged.

## Hints
- The cleanest predicate is `task.synthesizable` (added to TaskLike in T1.1).
  Avoid `instanceof` if the type guard works — keeps it open to future TaskLike
  implementations.
- This issue is small (~5 LOC change). The bulk of the work is reading
  `tekton-project.ts:103-117` and verifying nothing else needs updating.

## Depends on
- T1.1.
- T1.2 (Pipeline must already expose TaskLike-typed `allTasks`).

title: GitPipeline: skip workspace + stepTemplate injection for non-synthesizable TaskLikes
description:
## Why
`GitPipeline` mutates user tasks at construction time: it adds the shared
workspace to `task.workspaces` and injects `workingDir` into `task.stepTemplate`.
These mutations only make sense for `TaskDef` instances. For TaskRef-style nodes
they should be skipped (their workspaces are declared up-front by the user).

## What to change
- File: `src/lib/core/git-pipeline.ts`.
  - In the `allUserTasks.forEach(...)` block in the constructor (around line
    115), guard each mutation behind `if (!task.synthesizable) continue;`
    (or `instanceof TaskDef`).
  - `_discoverUserTasks` signature already updated in T1.2 — verify it returns
    `TaskLike[]` after this issue lands.

## Acceptance
- `flox activate -- npm test` — git-pipeline tests pass.
- A unit test that constructs a `GitPipeline` containing a stub non-synthesizable
  TaskLike does not throw and does not mutate the stub.

## Hints
- The stub TaskLike for the test can be a plain object: minimal `name`,
  `params: []`, `workspaces: []`, `needs: []`, `synthesizable: false`,
  `_toPipelineTaskSpec()` returning `{ name, taskRef: { kind: 'Task', name } }`.

## Depends on
- T1.1, T1.2, T1.3.

title: Epic: Pluggable cache backends (strategy pattern)
description:
## Why
`src/lib/core/task.ts` is a 670-line file that mixes the Task class with ~300
lines of nushell scripts for PVC and GCS cache restore/save. The
`if (backend.type === 'gcs')` branching means adding S3, Azure, or custom
backends requires editing `task.ts`. Apply the same pattern that `StatusReporter`
already proves: a strategy interface plus concrete implementations.

This both shrinks `task.ts` dramatically and turns "add another cache backend"
from a fork into a user-side extension.

Reference: `/Users/patrickfenerty/.claude/plans/evaluate-this-code-repoistory-federated-nest.md`,
priority #4.

## Scope
- Extract PVC script generation into `src/lib/cache/pvc-backend.ts`.
- Extract GCS script generation into `src/lib/cache/gcs-backend.ts`.
- Define `CacheBackend` strategy interface (`restoreStep`, `saveStep`).
- Convert `TaskDef` to delegate to backend methods.
- Document custom backend extension.

## Done when
- All four child issues closed.
- `task.ts` line count drops by ~300.
- `flox activate -- npm test` passes (no behavior change).
- A documented path for users to write their own `CacheBackend`.

title: Epic: Task results as first-class API
description:
## Why
Tekton Tasks declare typed `results` that downstream tasks consume via
`$(tasks.<name>.results.<name>)`. Tektonic has no API for results today —
`git-clone` writes metadata to a file on the workspace as a workaround. Without
results, cross-task data flow is not type-safe and hub-resolved tasks cannot
expose their declared results to consumers.

Reference: `/Users/patrickfenerty/.claude/plans/evaluate-this-code-repoistory-federated-nest.md`,
priority #2.

## Scope
- A `Result` class mirroring `Param`'s handle pattern.
- `results?: Result[]` on `TaskOptions` and emission in synthesized Task spec.
- Refactor `GitPipeline`'s git-clone to produce real Tekton results.

## Done when
- All three child issues closed.
- `flox activate -- npm test` passes (schema conformance test confirms `results`
  is a valid v1.TaskSpec field).

title: Epic: HubTaskRef + ArtifactHub interop
description:
## Why
ArtifactHub (formerly TektonHub) hosts a large catalog of community-maintained
Tasks. Tektonic should let users pull these in as nodes in their pipelines
without re-implementing them. This is the direct payoff of E1 (TaskLike) and
E2 (results) — together they make hub tasks fully type-safe participants.

Reference: `/Users/patrickfenerty/.claude/plans/evaluate-this-code-repoistory-federated-nest.md`,
priority #1 (interop) and #3.

## Scope
- `HubTaskRef` class implementing `TaskLike` with `synthesizable: false`.
- Emits a `taskRef` block using Tekton's hub resolver:
  ```yaml
  taskRef:
    resolver: hub
    params:
    - { name: catalog, value: tekton }
    - { name: name, value: git-clone }
    - { name: version, value: "0.9" }
  ```
- Schema conformance test for resolver-based pipeline-task entries.
- Example pipeline consuming a hub task end-to-end.

## Done when
- All three child issues closed.
- The example successfully synthesizes valid YAML.

## Depends on
- E1 (TaskLike interface required).

title: Detect breaking changes to core public API without knowing its providers
description:
Providers are unbounded (anyone can write one), so compatibility cannot be checked by testing each provider. Core checks its own published contract instead, in its own self-CI:
1. API report: committed report of the public surface (@tektonic-ci/core and /testing); CI fails when the built .d.ts no longer matches it, so every surface change is a reviewed diff.
2. Semver gate: on each PR, fetch @tektonic-ci/core@latest declarations from npm and compile a generated compat file asking tsc whether code written against the old version still works with the new one (extension points marked @extensionPoint: old implementation must satisfy new interface; values: new assignable to typeof old; types: both directions). A breaking result without a major bump in packages/tektonic/package.json fails the PR.
Supersedes the earlier plan of a per-provider job against core main.
acceptance_criteria: A PR that makes a breaking change to an export or extension point fails core self-CI unless packages/tektonic/package.json bumps the major; additive changes (e.g. a new optional interface member) pass; the check needs no knowledge of any provider.
notes:
2026-09-26: redesigned with user: no per-provider testing; provider list is unbounded. Layer 3 (behavioural conformance kit + next prerelease channel) split into its own issue.
PR #85: scripts/api-compat.mjs (report + compat vs @latest), check-api step in test-npm. Validated vs 2.1.0: required StatusReporter member fails, optional passes, removed export fails, removal passes at 3.0.0-rc.0. Gotcha: restoring a source with mv of an older backup leaves tsc -b dist stale; npm run clean before trusting api:update. Interfaces checked both ways, so no @extensionPoint tag needed.
Gate changed per user: breaking PR merges by declaring '### Breaking' under '## Unreleased' in CHANGELOG.md; release PR then passes only with a major bump (message says 'set the version to N.0.0'). CI fix: npm pack --json returned an object (not array) in the node image; baseline now fetched via npm view dist.tarball + fetch + in-process untar.
Found: typescript-api alias's tsc bin was linked over TS7's (.bin/tsc -> typescript-api), so local builds ran TS 5.9.3. Removed the alias; script now downloads typescript@5.9.3 into .api-compat and runs node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc (TS7) as judge with nodenext. Compat-file compile errors are now fatal, not waivable by a Breaking declaration. Re-validated under TS7; report unchanged.

title: tektonic synth leaves orphaned manifests behind (no --prune)
description: tektonic check reports orphans — files the project no longer emits — but tektonic synth does not remove them, so the only fix is deleting them by hand and check keeps failing until you do. Hit while removing the npm-release pipeline (tektonic-k2n.8): four manifests were left behind. Keep it opt-in: pruning deletes committed files, and an outdir shared with hand-written manifests would lose them.

title: Document and stabilise the task-factory/preset extension pattern
description:
Scope note: tektonic stays a foundation. Reusable job libraries are built ON it, not INTO it. This issue is about the seams such a library needs.

ocidex hand-rolled a small job library inside its own repo because there is no documented pattern for one: depScanTask (syft to grype to SARIF, jobs/_dep-scan.ts, an options-object task factory), uploadSarifStep (70 lines of nushell inside a TS template literal, shared.ts:164-237), buildImageTask (jobs/image-build/spec.ts), plus pacBaseline and a git-safe-directory preamble in script-lib.ts. Every ocidex task also restates statusReporter, computeResources and env sets by hand.

Nothing about these is ocidex-specific, but nothing in tektonic says the options-object-to-Task factory is a supported extension shape, or which types are stable to build on.
design: Document the task-factory/preset pattern with a worked example (the depScan shape is the natural one). Audit the public surface for the types such a factory needs — TaskStepSpec, TaskCacheSpec, TaskSidecarSpec, ScriptInput, StatusReporter — and commit to their stability. Consider project-level task defaults so presets do not have to restate statusReporter and resources. Add a docs page: building a job library on tektonic, covering the exit-code contract and status-reporter wiring as part of the public contract.
acceptance_criteria: A second consumer can write a depScanTask-equivalent by following the docs, without reading tektonic internals. ocidex job library could move to its own package unchanged.

title: Add a serial-chain / concurrency primitive
description:
ocidex hand-rolls serialChain() (jobs/image-build/spec.ts:253-260): a loop that makes task[i] depend on task[i-1] so eleven image builds run one at a time rather than overcommitting the single CI worker. The comment records why — parallel builds leave pods Pending with Insufficient cpu, and the shared buildkit root makes serial order actively cheap.

Serialising a set of tasks to fit node capacity is generic scheduling, not an application concern, and it is easy to get subtly wrong (the chain must be rebuilt per pipeline since ocidex needs two: image-build and image-release).
design: Add a primitive that takes a list of tasks and returns them chained, or expresses a concurrency limit over a group. Keep it composable with needs so a chain can itself depend on upstream tasks (ocidex chains carry needs: [goTest, goIntegration, openapiCheck] on every element).
acceptance_criteria: ocidex serialChain helper is replaced by a library call, for both the push and tag chains.

title: Make the exit-code contract un-loseable: error on exit in capturing bodies, explicit raw-shebang opt-out
description:
Two ways a consumer silently loses the exit-code contract:

1. exit N inside a nushell body. nushell exit is untrappable, so it kills the process before the wrapper persists the code to the contract file, which keeps its initial 0; with onError: continue on the step, the task reports GREEN ON REAL FAILURE. This shipped in ocidex own drift check and is recorded at length in .tektonic/jobs/tekton-check/spec.ts — the report-only rollout exit signal was worthless because the body used exit 1. Bodies must use error make instead. v1.3.0 (tektonic-ntj) added a lint WARNING; a warning is not enough for a failure mode whose symptom is a green check.

2. A raw string starting with #! is passed through verbatim with no wrapper (task.ts / renderScript), so it silently opts out of exit-code capture. ocidex uploadSarifStep relies on exactly this (shared.ts:180-184 comment) — legitimately, but the opt-out is a side effect of how the string begins rather than a stated intent.
design: Make exit in a capturing body an error by default (escape hatch for the rare deliberate case), and make the raw-shebang path an explicit typed opt-out (e.g. a rawScript() wrapper or a step flag) so it reads as a decision at the call site. Expose the linter to consumers through the CLI so they can enforce it too.
acceptance_criteria: A nushell body containing exit 1 in a reporting task fails synth with a message pointing at error make. Passing a shebang string without the explicit opt-out is rejected.

title: Dedent-safe script fragment composition and supported sh-in-nu embedding
description:
Consumers compose script bodies out of shared fragments, and today that is convention plus comments rather than API. ocidex .tektonic/script-lib.ts opens with a note that its snippets are interpolated into tektonic nu templates flush-left at column 0 so the tag dedent leaves them clean — i.e. fragment indentation is load-bearing and unchecked.

memoryWatchdog (script-lib.ts:36-63) shows the harder case: a POSIX sh body embedded in a nushell script via sh -c, where nushell values cannot be interpolated across the boundary, so callers smuggle them through as positional args read back as "$@" inside the sh body. The comment spells out that the watchdog body is a raw string, so nushell interpolation is unavailable there by design. Other comments record adjacent traps: interpolated nu strings must not contain bare parentheses (shared.ts:210-213); command substitution $(...) collides with Tekton own $(...) syntax (git-pipeline.ts:126-128, script-lib.ts:68-70).
design: Provide a fragment/compose primitive that normalises indentation when a fragment is interpolated at any depth, so fragments need not be authored flush-left. Provide a supported primitive for embedding a foreign-language body inside a script (sh inside nu being the driving case) with explicit argument passing, so callers stop hand-rolling $@ smuggling. Document the bare-parenthesis and $(...) collision rules next to it.
acceptance_criteria: ocidex script-lib.ts fragments can be indented naturally, and memoryWatchdog is expressed through the embedding primitive rather than a raw string.

title: Export typed handles for PAC well-known params and workspace subpaths
description:
tektonic has typed primitives — Workspace.path, Param, Result.path — but consumers still hand-write Tekton variable strings all over their job specs. In ocidex: the literal $(workspaces.workspace.path) appears in shared.ts:79/125 and in the image-build, helm-publish, gh-release and openapi-check specs; $(params.revision), $(params.source-branch) and $(params.repo-full-name) appear inside script bodies in shared.ts:164-237 and image-build/spec.ts.

The PAC-injected well-known params (url, revision, project-name, repo-full-name, source-branch) are defined in tektonic-project.ts:65-77 and bound automatically, but are not exported as typed handles at all — so a consumer that wants the source branch must both declare a matching Param by hand (ocidex sourceBranchParam, shared.ts:157) and interpolate the raw string in the script. A typo is a runtime template that never substitutes.
design: Export the well-known params as constants (e.g. PAC_PARAMS.revision / sourceBranch / repoFullName) that consumers can put straight in a task params array and interpolate into script templates via the existing Param toString. Add a workspace subpath helper so ws.at(.go-mod) beats string concatenation.
acceptance_criteria: ocidex can delete sourceBranchParam and replace every raw $(params.*) / $(workspaces.*) literal in .tektonic with a typed reference.

title: Export consumer test helpers (synthToObjects + graph assertions)
description:
Consumers have no way to unit-test their pipeline definitions. ocidex verifies behaviour by submitting ad-hoc TaskRuns against the live cluster — see the tekton-check spec comment recording that both polarities were verified by ad-hoc TaskRun: clean tree Succeeded, injected un-synthed source bump StepFailed with exit-code=1. That is a slow, manual loop for what should be a vitest assertion.

tektonic already has the machinery internally (schema-validation.test.ts, pipeline.test.ts) but exports none of it.
design: Export a synthToObjects(project) style helper returning the parsed manifests in memory, plus small assertions over the graph: task present/absent, runAfter edges, effective when clause, params bound. Document a worked example: assert that a frontend-only PR skips the Go tasks.
acceptance_criteria: A consumer can write a vitest test asserting gating behaviour without writing YAML to disk or touching a cluster.

title: gated() does not auto-wire Condition.sources() the way Task.when does
description:
TaskDef constructor auto-wires the producing tasks of a when Condition into needs (task.ts:426-432). gated() does not — its overrides are applied only at _toPipelineTaskSpec time (pipeline-task.ts:78-96), so nothing pulls the producing task into the pipeline.

ocidex therefore maintains the detection tasks by hand: .tektonic/changes.ts:64-70 builds a detectTasks array by calling .sources() on all five onChanges conditions and spreading it into the PR pipeline, with a comment explaining that gated() overrides only the emitted when and does not auto-wire the producing task. Forgetting an entry produces a pipeline referencing a result no task in it produces.
design: Once the overlay refactor lands (see the gated() identity issue), Pipeline can walk overlay conditions and call Condition.sources() during discovery, exactly as TaskDef does for its own when. Keep .sources() public for consumers who want explicit control.
acceptance_criteria: A PR pipeline listing only gated(task, { when: onChangesCondition }) synthesizes with the detection task present. ocidex can delete the detectTasks array.

title: TektonicProject silently collapses same-named tasks across pipelines
description:
TektonicProject collects tasks into a Map keyed by name, first-wins, across all pipelines (tektonic-project.ts:217-223). Every GitPipeline generates its own git-clone Task, so a project with three GitPipelines has three distinct git-clone objects; only the first is synthesized, and all three PipelineRuns reference it by taskRef name. Any divergence in cloneDepth, cloneImage or chainsProvenance is silently discarded — the pipeline runs YAML it did not declare.

ocidex already reasons around this by hand at .tektonic/pipeline.ts:48-51: all three pipelines share one generated git-clone task, so clone depth must be consistent. That constraint is invisible in the type system and enforced only by a comment.
design: When two tasks share a name, compare their synthesized specs. Identical: dedupe as today. Divergent: throw with both task names, the owning pipelines, and a diff of the differing fields. Optionally offer per-pipeline name prefixing as the escape hatch.
acceptance_criteria: Two GitPipelines with different cloneDepth in one TektonicProject fail synth with a clear message instead of emitting one pipeline silently running the other clone config.

title: Skip-resolver never POSTs: $(tasks.X.status) is not substituted in step scripts
description:
createSkipResolverTask embeds $(tasks.<name>.status) directly in the nushell step script. Tekton substitutes that variable in a PipelineTask's params/when but NOT inside a referenced Task's step script, so at runtime $status is the literal string, never equals "None", and the success/Skipped POST is unreachable for every context. Verified on ocidex PR #104 (contexts stuck pending forever) and by two ad-hoc PipelineRun probes.

Fix: declare one Param per entry with pipelineExpression: '$(tasks.<taskName>.status)' (the mechanism already exists in core/param.ts and is documented for exactly this case) and read $(params.status-<taskName>) in skipResolverScript.

Secondary: each resolve step ends catch { exit 1 }, and Tekton skips all remaining steps in a pod after a non-zero step, so one failed POST swallows every later context. Same shape in createPendingTask. Add onError: continue to both.

Downstream: ocidex ocidex-6rbk.
notes:
Files: src/lib/reporters/github-status-reporter.ts (statusParam helper, createSkipResolverTask params + onError, skipResolverScript signature), src/index.ts (export statusParam), tests in github-status-reporter.test.ts + core/pipeline.test.ts.
Approach: status travels as a Param carrying pipelineExpression $(tasks.<taskName>.status), which Tekton substitutes in the finally PipelineTask's params; the script reads $(params.status-<taskName>). Param keyed on taskName (contexts may contain /). onError: continue added to resolve and pending steps so a failed POST does not skip the remaining steps in the pod.
Verified: 364 unit tests green; ad-hoc PipelineRun probe-resolver-dph4j in ocidex-ci showed skipped task -> 'task was skipped, POST ...' and ran task -> 'task status is Succeeded', with step 1 exiting 1 (404 to a nonexistent repo) and all 7 later steps still running.

title: exit-code contract file is unwritable by steps that override runAsUser
description:
The first wrapped step of a reporting task creates $(EXIT_CODE_PATH) with mode 0644 owned by the pod's default uid. A later step with its own securityContext.runAsUser (e.g. moby/buildkit:rootless at uid 1000) can read the file but not write it, so its exit code is silently dropped and the status reporter reads the earlier step's 0 -> a failing step reports success.

Observed in ocidex: every image-build/image-release TaskRun logs 'can't create /tekton/home/.exit-code: Permission denied' from the buildkit step, then 'report-status: exit-code=0 state=success'.

Fix: in each ScriptLanguage.wrap(), when captureExitCode is true, emit a prologue that creates the file seeded with 0 if absent and best-effort chmods it 0666, so any later uid can write it.

Parent epic: plan-8ws. Downstream consumer: ocidex-f2bj.
notes:
Files: src/lib/script/{sh,nushell,python,types}.ts + matching .test.ts
Approach: capturing wrap() now emits a two-line prologue before the body — create EXIT_CODE_PATH seeded with 0 if absent, then best-effort chmod 0666 — so a step with its own runAsUser can write the file the first step created. Seeded with 0 rather than empty because sh's numeric worst-of comparison breaks on an empty prev. Verified on the ocidex-ci cluster with paired throwaway TaskRuns (uid 1024 step + uid 1000 buildkit step exiting 7): pre-fix VERDICT exit-code=0 with 'Permission denied' and mode -rw-r--r--; post-fix VERDICT exit-code=7 with mode -rw-rw-rw-. Released as v1.2.1.

title: Epic: 'when' clause support for conditional task execution
description:
## Why
Tekton supports `when` expressions on pipeline tasks for conditional execution.
Today the only way to express "run X only on PRs" in Tektonic is to write a
separate pipeline per trigger. As pipelines grow this multiplies combinatorially.
Adding `when` is the single biggest unlock for the "dynamic logic" half of your
goal.

Reference: `/Users/patrickfenerty/.claude/plans/evaluate-this-code-repoistory-federated-nest.md`,
priority #5.

## Scope
- A `WhenExpression` type.
- A way to attach `when` to a task as it participates in a pipeline (NOT on the
  Task definition itself, since the same task can have different `when` clauses
  in different pipelines).
- Emission into pipeline task spec.
- Schema conformance.

## Open design question
Where does `when` live? Two reasonable options:

1. Per-task option (simple): `new Task({ ..., when: [...] })`. Easy but tightly
   couples a task instance to one pipeline use case.
2. Per-pipeline-edge option (flexible): wrap the task at the pipeline call site,
   e.g. `pipeline.tasks: [test, gated(build, { when: [...] })]`. Lets the same
   `build` task be conditional in one pipeline and unconditional in another.

Pick option 2 for flexibility — it matches Tekton's own model and composes well
with future features like per-pipeline `retries` and `timeout`. Reserve option 1
as the convenience shorthand if needed later.

## Done when
- Both child issues closed.
- Schema conformance test for `when` passes.

A repo with both a push pipeline and a TAG pipeline therefore runs both on a tag push. Noticed while adding the npm-release pipeline in examples/self-ci.ts (tektonic-k2n.8). description: Follow-up to tektonic-k2n.3, which implemented (a) atomic staged restore and (b) synth-time shared-workspace detection defaulting skipRestoreIfPathsExist. Part (c) of that issue's design is unimplemented: consumers still hand-derive one cache spec per task (ocidex had goCache/goCacheTest/goCacheVulncheck/goCacheIntegration) differing only in skipRestoreIfPathsExist/forceSave. A single declaration naming one producer task and N consumers would emit the right restore/save behaviour per task from one object.

title: TaskSidecarSpec parity: volumeMounts, ScriptInput, inherited pull policy
description:
TaskSidecarSpec (task.ts:197-234) lags TaskStepSpec in three ways that ocidex hit while adding the integration-test sidecars (jobs/go-integration/spec.ts):
- No volumeMounts. The postgres sidecar comment records that PGDATA lands on the container writable layer, so it needs an ephemeral-storage limit rather than a volume, and notes this also sidesteps TaskSidecarSpec having no volumeMounts.
- script is string, not ScriptInput, so sidecar bodies get none of the language tagging, dedenting or lint support that step scripts get.
- Tekton applies stepTemplate to steps only, so the project defaultImagePullPolicy does not reach sidecars; both ocidex sidecars restate imagePullPolicy: Always with a comment explaining why. tektonic documents this but could stamp it instead.
design: Add volumeMounts to TaskSidecarSpec, widen script to ScriptInput, and have TektonicProject apply defaultImagePullPolicy to sidecars directly since stepTemplate cannot. Keep the per-sidecar override.
acceptance_criteria: ocidex sidecars drop their restated imagePullPolicy, and a sidecar can mount a task volume.

title: PAC event context as a first-class project option
description:
To let steps see the PAC event context, ocidex adds raw podTemplateEnv entries mapping PAC template variables into the pod (.tektonic/pipeline.ts:166-170): PAC_EVENT_TYPE from event_type and PAC_TARGET_BRANCH from target_branch. Its security scans then read those to decide between a diff-scoped and a full scan (script-lib.ts:71-78, pacBaseline).

Knowing that these PAC variables exist, that they are substituted before submission, and that podTemplateEnv is where they go, is undocumented tribal knowledge. The same block also carries an unrelated HOME workaround, which is itself a finding: a project-wide runAsUser with no passwd entry breaks Tekton creds-init unless HOME is set to /tekton/home.
design: Add an opt-in project option that injects the PAC event context under stable names, and document the HOME /tekton/home requirement (or set it automatically) when defaultPodSecurityContext sets a runAsUser with no passwd entry.
acceptance_criteria: ocidex can drop the two PAC env entries and the HOME workaround from podTemplateEnv.

title: Compile or() of onChanges into one union detection task (no CEL flag)
description:
or(goChanged, nodeChanged) composes into a CEL when-expression, which requires the enable-cel-in-whenexpression Tekton feature flag — off on the homelab cluster. So ocidex hand-maintains a THIRD detection task whose paths are the union of the other two, purely to gate multi-language semgrep with a classic in guard (.tektonic/changes.ts:36-43, detect-source). The union must be kept in sync with goChanged and nodeChanged by hand.

This is mechanically derivable: an or() over onChanges conditions is exactly one detection task whose pathspecs are the union of the operands.
design: Detect that every operand of an or() is an onChanges condition and, when so, synthesize a single union detection task and gate on its result with a classic in clause. Fall back to CEL for heterogeneous or()s. Document which shapes avoid the feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: or(onChanges(a), onChanges(b)) emits one detection task with the union pathspec and a non-CEL when clause. ocidex can delete detect-source.

title: Pending-status task assumes a single StatusReporter for all contexts
description:
Pipeline picks statusTasks[0].statusReporter and uses that one instance to build the set-status-pending task for EVERY reporting context in the pipeline (pipeline.ts:94-98). The same first-wins assumption applies to createSkipResolverTask (pipeline.ts:104).

ocidex has two reporter instances — statusReporter and reportOnlyStatusReporter, which differ in failOnError (.tektonic/shared.ts:28-48) — and only gets away with it because both are GitHubStatusReporter posting to the same API with the same token. A project mixing a GitHub reporter with, say, a Slack or GitLab one would silently report every context through whichever task happened to be discovered first.
design: Group reporting tasks by reporter instance and emit one pending task (and one skip resolver) per reporter. Name them per-reporter to keep task names unique.
acceptance_criteria: A pipeline with two distinct StatusReporter implementations emits a pending task for each, and each context is initialised through its own reporter.

title: Add imagePullPolicy support: project default + per-step/sidecar override
description:
No way to set imagePullPolicy on a Tekton step or sidecar from tektonic. TaskStepSpec/TaskSidecarSpec have no such field, and there is no project-level default. Consumers referencing mutable image tags (ocidex: base:stable x161, moby/buildkit:rootless x20) get the kubelet's IfNotPresent default, so a republished tag is served from node cache indefinitely with no signal.

Add: exported ImagePullPolicy type; optional imagePullPolicy on TaskStepSpec and TaskSidecarSpec (pure passthrough); defaultImagePullPolicy on TektonicProjectOptions, threaded into TaskDef.synth and merged into each task's stepTemplate before the task's own stepTemplate spread.

title: Name the task and step in the script catch line
description:
nushell.ts:41 prints 'error: ($e.msg)', which for a failed external command yields the anonymous 'error: External command had a non-zero exit code' — no task, no step, no command. For report-only tasks (failOnError: false) that log line plus the check colour is the ONLY signal, which is what made ocidex-qzz2 invisible for a day.

Carry the task and step name on ScriptCtx (src/lib/script/types.ts) and interpolate them so the line reads 'error [<task>/<step>]: ...'. Apply the same to Sh/Bash for consistency. Fixes the signal once in the framework instead of once per consumer task.
acceptance_criteria: Rendered nu and sh wrappers include the task/step name in the catch/failure line; unit tests assert it.

Nushell's catch prints `error [t/s]: ($e.msg)`; Sh/Bash gained a failure line entirely (they printed nothing on a non-zero body). Names are Kubernetes names so they cannot introduce parentheses that nushell would evaluate inside an interpolated string. Commit 
567eb5e.

title: Reject bare 'exit' in nushell bodies at synth time
description:
The lint ocidex-foif asks for, implemented where it cannot be bypassed. nushell's 'exit' kills the process before the try/catch wrapper persists the code, so a body using 'exit 1' reports green (ocidex-es6). A consumer-side grep misses scriptFromFile bodies and only fires in CI.

In Nushell.wrap, when ctx.captureExitCode is true, scan the body for a top-level 'exit' AFTER stripping r#'...'# raw-string blocks — those legitimately contain 'exit' (ocidex's go-vulncheck watchdog embeds a POSIX sh script that way). Throw with a message naming 'error make' as the replacement. Fires during 'make tekton-synth' in dev rather than in CI.

Downgrade to a warning if tektonic-9wr lands, since 'exit' then behaves correctly.
acceptance_criteria: A nu body with a bare 'exit 1' throws at synth; the same text inside r#'...'# does not; the thrown message names error make.
notes:
Files: src/lib/script/nushell.ts (warnOnExit), src/lib/script/nushell.test.ts.
Approach: implemented as a WARNING, not the throw the issue originally specified — the issue's own last line said to downgrade if tektonic-9wr landed, and it did. After 9wr the reporter reads Tekton's per-step exitCode, so 'exit 1' is reported correctly; the only remaining cost is that the process dies before the catch, losing the 'error [task/step]' attribution line.
Narrowed to NON-ZERO exits. A hard ban on all 'exit' would have been a false positive on correct ocidex code: uploadSarifStep's trailing 'exit 0' and push-sboms.nu:7's unset-API-key skip are both legitimate early returns that cannot hide a failure. Raw strings r#'...'# are stripped before scanning (go-vulncheck's embedded sh watchdog's 'exit 99' is correct for its interpreter). Verified zero warnings against ocidex's .tektonic sources.
Commit $(git rev-parse --short HEAD).

title: Read Tekton's per-step exitCode files in finalStep
description:
Root cause of the ocidex-es6 class: tektonic maintains /tekton/home/.exit-code INSIDE the script (src/lib/script/nushell.ts:36-45), so nushell's untrappable 'exit' bypasses it and report-status reads a stale 0. Sh dodges this with a subshell (sh.ts:41-48); nushell cannot, so the capture must move out of the script.

Verified on a real cluster (2026-08-10, rpi-cluster/ocidex-ci): Tekton writes /tekton/steps/step-<name>/exitCode for EVERY completed step — not only failed ones, and regardless of whether onError is set. Mode 0644 (readable across uids), absent only for the currently-running step, which is the reporter's own position.

Change finalScript to take the max of the existing .exit-code file AND the per-step files for the user steps, so a body calling 'exit 1' is reported correctly and nothing regresses if a file is absent.

Do NOT glob /tekton/steps/*/exitCode: the injected cache save/restore steps also carry onError: continue, and a failed cache save must stay non-fatal. Pass the user step names explicitly — widen the interface to finalStep(context: string, userStepNames?: string[]) in src/lib/core/status-reporter.ts, mirroring the optional-method pattern already used for createSkipResolverTask?, so external implementations keep compiling. TaskDef.synth has the names in scope at the reporterStep construction site (src/lib/core/task.ts:463-490).
acceptance_criteria: finalScript reads the per-step exitCode files for user steps only; a nu body using 'exit 1' is reported as a failure; a failed cache save-step still does not fail the task; unit tests in github-status-reporter.test.ts cover all three.
notes:
Files: src/lib/script/types.ts (stepExitCodePath), src/lib/script/index.ts (re-export), src/lib/core/status-reporter.ts (finalStep signature), src/lib/core/task.ts (pass user step names), src/lib/reporters/github-status-reporter.ts (finalScript), + tests.

Approach: finalScript now computes max(contract file, per-step exitCode files for user steps only). Kept the contract file as a second source so a Tekton that does not write per-step files degrades to the old behaviour instead of reporting blanket success. Step names passed explicitly rather than globbing /tekton/steps — the injected cache SAVE step carries onError: continue so a failed cache write is non-fatal, and consulting it would overturn that (the restore step does not carry onError, verified in test).

Cluster probe (rpi-cluster/ocidex-ci, 2026-08-10): /tekton/steps/step-<name>/exitCode is a symlink to /tekton/run/<idx>/status/exitCode, written for EVERY completed step regardless of onError, mode 0644, absent only for the currently-running step. Also verified the nu aggregation in real nushell 0.113: stale contract 0 + step 3 -> 3; empty step list -> parses; missing contract -> 1 (preserves existing semantics).
